modifications: Converted from TEI XML to plain text paragraphs with emphasis, with the long s printed as s. Each exposition opens with the words of the text it expounds as Fergusson printed them, such as Vers. 1. PAUL an Apostle, and the paragraphs after a quotation stay with its verse. On Galatians to Colossians each exposition the transcription divides off is one section, keyed by the verse label printed at its head, such as Vers. 1. or Vers.—22., and two expositions that open on the same verse, where a quotation resumes a verse, share its section. Ephesians 1:6, printed 5, is read as the verse its text quotes. On Thessalonians each quotation's label opens a section, and a label misprinted between two that follow on is read as the number between them, as 1 Thessalonians 2:6, printed 10. A verse named in an argument or in the exposition, such as v. 23., is never read. A section runs from its own verse to the verse before the next section or the end of its chapter. An epistle's argument and a chapter's opening analysis open its first section. Every gap the transcribers could not key is kept as the mark they gave it, such as • for an illegible letter and 〈◊〉 for an illegible word. Line-end hyphens are closed up. Left out: the title pages, the dedication, the epistles to the reader, the errata, the headings such as CHAP. I., and the notes on the postscripts that close the epistles to the Thessalonians.
